To understand how a CPU cache works, you first have to understand the **"Memory Wall."** 

Modern CPUs are incredibly fast, but RAM (System Memory) is relatively slow. If a CPU had to wait for RAM every time it needed a piece of data, it would spend 95% of its time sitting idle. The **Cache** is a small, ultra-fast memory buffer located directly on the CPU chip designed to bridge this speed gap.
